dedupe_keys.name: maximal load delivery for damaged natural gas pipeline networks mixed integer convex relaxation and multi contingency analysis

description: This record describes a 2020 arXiv paper on determining a feasible steady-state operating point for a damaged natural gas pipeline network while delivering as much load as possible. Electric power systems increasingly depend on gas-fired plants as fast-ramping sources, so disruption of gas transmission, from natural or man-made disasters, becomes a power system vulnerability. The authors formulate the mixed-integer nonconvex maximal load delivery (MLD) problem, which is hard on large networks, and present a mixed-integer convex relaxation that gives bounds on the transport capacity of a gas pipeline system. Exact and relaxed formulations are compared across many randomised damage scenarios on nine network models with 11 to 4,197 junctions, and a proof of concept applies synthetically generated earthquakes to show the optimisation-based capacity evaluation for risk assessment. Coverage is nine gas network models and synthetic damage scenarios. Access: the paper PDF on arXiv, free; no code or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: a steady-state formulation, so transients are not covered. It suits gas network resilience and interdependency studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
